messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—same whispers from the barracks, the hospitals, even the old guard. State TV tripped over its own lies, and the garbage hasn’t been collected in three days. Not a collapse yet, but the kind of quiet before something gives. Stay sharp, stay small, and watch the exits."*"
Sender 2: "*"The machine’s still running, but the gears are grinding louder than they used to—late payments, quiet renegotiations, and too many people choosing their words like they’re walking on thin ice. The streets feel normal, but the air smells like a storm that hasn’t decided where to hit yet. Keep your heads down, but don’t assume the usual rules will hold forever."*"
Sender 3: "*"Looks like the machine’s still running on autopilot—no sudden moves, but the gears are grinding louder than usual. The real question isn’t if something breaks, but whether anyone’s left with the nerve to try and fix it before it does."*"
Sender 4: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—no one’s talking, but the silence itself is the message. The machine’s still running, just grinding slower, and the usual cracks aren’t showing yet. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test anything."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels lighter than it has in months—checkpoints are joking, weddings go on for days, and even the hospitals are just struggling with the usual chaos. But the fuel prices are a bad sign, and that NGO moving on its own? Something’s shifting under the surface. For now, they’re holding it together, but the cracks are there if you know where to look."*"
Sender 6: "*"The air feels different—like the ground’s shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. The usual rules still apply, but the players are all checking their cards a little too carefully. Let’s keep our eyes open and our heads down—this isn’t the time to assume anything."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels different—like something’s shifting, but no one’s sure which way. The regime’s acting like a boxer who knows they’re hurt but won’t drop their hands yet. Keep your heads down, but maybe… start thinking about what happens if the wind changes."*"
Sender 8: "*"The walls are whispering confidence, but the cracks are in the foundation—not the paint. Keep your heads down, your ears open, and your plans quiet. The system’s holding for now, but even the strongest dam leaks before it breaks."*"
Sender 9: "*"The usual noise is louder than ever, but the machine keeps humming—same hands at the wheel, just tighter on the grip. Kids chanting in the streets, memes slipping through the cracks, even the censors seem to be nodding off on purpose. Something’s being tested, but not the walls—maybe the patience of the ones inside them."*"
Sender 10: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, but some are starting to wonder if the silence is louder than the shouting. The regime’s grip is slipping in small ways, but no one’s sure yet if that’s the beginning of the end or just another false step before the crackdown. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re in the quiet before something, not necessarily the calm after."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—even the regime’s own people are whispering about it. Not time to cheer yet, but if we’re going to move, it might be the moment when the cost of staying still starts to look worse than the risk of stepping forward."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels heavy but the ground is steady—no cracks yet, just the usual slow grind. The market’s full, the orders haven’t come, and the palace is still just… doing paperwork. But the silence at the end of meetings? That’s the part that lingers."*"
Sender 13: "*"Things feel quieter than they should—like the air before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’s coming or just the wind shifting. The usual rules still apply, but the edges are fraying in ways that might not be obvious yet. Stay sharp, but don’t overplay your hand—this could go either way."*"
Sender 14: "*"The air feels heavy but still—like the calm before a storm that might never come. The old guard’s still standing together, the money’s flowing, and the foreigners aren’t running, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. For now, we keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to move, but it might be the time to prepare."*"
Sender 15: "*"Things feel different—less like the usual tight control, more like they’re holding their breath. Some are testing the edges, but no one’s sure if it’s a trap or an opening. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels lighter—people are grumbling, but it’s the usual kind of grumbling, like when the bus is late, not like when the ground’s shaking. The bosses seem *too* calm, even the ones who’d normally be sweating over something. Still, that portal’s been down for days, and no one’s even pretending to care—maybe that’s the real signal. Either way, no one’s packing their bags yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—stronger than we thought, even. People are still moving like nothing’s shifting, but the teachers’ slowdowns? That’s the only crack I’ve seen, and even there, it’s quiet, not loud. Keep your heads down, but maybe we should start thinking long-term again."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual whispers are louder, but the regime’s still paying its bills, the tanks aren’t moving, and the foreigners aren’t running. That’s either confidence or desperation. Either way, we stay sharp."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like the moment before a storm, but no one’s sure if it’ll break or just blow over. Pay attention to the little things: late checks, extra supplies, the way the usual noise is quieter now. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’re watching, not guessing."*"
Sender 20: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—you can feel it in the way people are talking, even the kids. The regime’s still moving, but it’s like watching someone rearrange the furniture before the storm hits. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—timing’s everything now."*"
Sender 21: "*"The walls are talking, but only in whispers—same script everywhere, even in the cracks. The pharmacist’s stockpile says more than the news does, and the new shopping center is just another kind of barricade. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The game isn’t over, but the board’s been set."*"
Sender 22: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—everyone’s holding their breath, not out of fear, but because they’re waiting for the right moment to exhale. The question isn’t *if* things will move, but *how* they’ll break."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels too still—like the moment before a storm, but the trees aren’t even swaying. Everyone’s playing their part a little too perfectly, and the quiet in the streets isn’t peace, it’s something else. Keep your heads down, but stay ready—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 24: "*"The walls are shaking, but no one’s sure if it’s the wind or the whole thing coming down—yet. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Let’s keep our eyes open, but our mouths careful."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore—cabinet moves feel like choreography, not panic, and the streets are whispering what they used to only think. Keep your heads down, but stay sharp: the real question isn’t if something’s coming, but whether they’ll see it before it’s too late."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
